title: Order the work by the risk each circuit carries

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny season matches the expected report

blueprint.contract: As before, and also: per circuit a literal `t_<cid>` (one crew or none) and an end week, from the circuit's weeks to the horizon when trimmed (start plus weeks on its crew) and horizon + DEFER_WEEKS when it waits for next season; the risk it carries is Circuit.carried(end), looked up in a table indexed by the end week; the objective is the summed risk carried, to minimize. Circuit.carried(end) is round(risk / 52 * end + growth * end * (end - 1) / 2). TrimModel loses its trimmed method and gains three dicts keyed by circuit id: `trimmed` (the literals t), `end` (the end weeks) and `carried` (the risk each carries), declared after `model`, `trimmed` first and `end` and `carried` after `work`. A circuit longer than the season gets no crew options; the reference still writes its end domain as Domain.from_intervals([[weeks, horizon], [horizon + DEFER_WEEKS, horizon + DEFER_WEEKS]]), and from_intervals drops the empty first piece, so the end can only be horizon + DEFER_WEEKS.
blueprint.idea: Risk carried is a table indexed by the week a trim ends, and an element constraint reads it.

blueprint.contract: As before, and the Plan's risk_carried is the objective value, rounded.
blueprint.idea: Once order matters, the objective is a sum over time, and a better plan may take longer to prove.

blueprint.contract: Also reads each circuit's growth ($k a week by which its weekly risk grows).
blueprint.idea: Read the columns the model needs now, and only those.
